entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Charles Gérard Eyschen (1821–1886) was a Luxembourgish politician and lawyer who served in Luxembourg's Chamber of Deputies and helped develop the constitutional and legal framework of independent Luxembourg after the 1839 Treaty of London established Luxembourg's definitive boundaries and guaranteed its neutrality. Luxembourgish politics in this era were shaped by the grand duchy's complex position — nominally in personal union with the Netherlands under the House of Orange-Nassau yet constitutionally autonomous and neutral, part of the German Confederation yet culturally French. The 1848 revolutions brought a more liberal constitution to Luxembourg, creating the parliamentary framework within which Eyschen worked.

His son Paul Eyschen would serve as Luxembourg's Prime Minister for a remarkable 27 years (1888–1915) — one of Europe's longest-serving prime ministers.

His career contributed to Luxembourg's early constitutional governance.

He was a significant Luxembourgish legal and political figure.
